subject: Estimating moth densities from goal post counts

messages.author: f5e868a025d2241c
messages.subject: Estimating moth densities from goal post counts
parts:
Hi,

Although this is not strictly Distance related, I'm hoping some of you may
be able to provide some feedback or leads.

We're hoping to estimate densities of moths flying over crop fields at
night. We have some counts of moth numbers that pass through "goal posts"
set in the field and observed over set intervals with night vision goggles.
The goal posts are set 5 metres apart and 4 metres high. We also have data
on average moth flight speed and wind velocity. Unfortunately we cannot
follow individual moths very far before they are lost from sight, and we
don't know what proportion of the moths are 'passing through' and what
proportion may be 'resident' within the field boundaries.

Has anyone applied similar methods for other mobile creatures (bats ? birds
? marine creatures ? other insects ?). Are there any standard formulas for
estimating densities from such counts ? Finally, does anyone have any
comments or suggestions on this technique ?

Thanks in advance,
Martin
